Generate sequences from a fitted transition tree

Source: R/predict.R
generate_sequences.Rd

generate_sequences() draws new sequences from the process described by a fitted tree. Each sequence starts from a state drawn from the overall distribution of states (or from a given first state), and each further state is drawn from the next-state distribution of the longest context of the tree that matches the states generated so far. Generated sequences can be compared with the observed ones to check whether the tree reproduces features of the data that it was not fitted to directly, such as run lengths or the time spent in each state.

Draws use the session's random number generator; call set.seed() first, or use simulate.transitiontrees() with seed, for reproducible sequences. It returns one sequence per row, as a character matrix or, with tidy = TRUE, a data frame.

Usage

generate_sequences(tree, n = 5L, length = 10L, start = NULL, tidy = FALSE)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

n

Number of sequences. Default 5.

length

Number of states in each sequence. Default 10.

start

First state of each sequence, a character vector of length n. NULL (default) draws it from the root distribution.

tidy

Return a data.frame rather than a matrix. Default FALSE.

Value

With tidy = TRUE, a data.frame with one row per sequence and columns T1 to T<length>, which context_tree() accepts as input. With tidy = FALSE, a character matrix with the same layout.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree, n or length is not a single positive number, or start does not have length n.

See also

simulate.transitiontrees(), predict.transitiontrees().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
set.seed(1)
generate_sequences(tree, n = 5, length = 12, tidy = TRUE)
#>           T1         T2      T3         T4         T5         T6         T7
#> 1    Average Disengaged Average    Average     Active     Active     Active
#> 2    Average Disengaged Average    Average    Average    Average    Average
#> 3     Active     Active  Active Disengaged Disengaged Disengaged Disengaged
#> 4 Disengaged    Average Average    Average    Average     Active     Active
#> 5    Average    Average  Active    Average     Active    Average    Average
#>           T8         T9        T10     T11     T12
#> 1     Active     Active     Active  Active  Active
#> 2 Disengaged Disengaged Disengaged Average Average
#> 3 Disengaged    Average    Average Average Average
#> 4    Average    Average     Active  Active Average
#> 5    Average    Average    Average Average Average
